title: Safe auto-apply for Optimize suggestions: gated rollouts, canaries, and approvals
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Goal: Implement a safe auto-apply path for Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching and KV/prefix caching config changes) that allows automated recommendation application while guaranteeing rollback and operational controls. This ticket covers the engineering design and initial implementation for gated rollouts, canary policies, and an approval workflow integrated with Console and Slack.

Background: Optimize already computes workload-specific suggestions (batch size tweaks, cache window sizes, and cache key strategies) based on historical token distributions and KV-hit simulations. Customers have asked for a way to safely apply high-confidence recommendations automatically to reduce unit cost, while minimizing risk to latency SLOs and output quality.

Scope (what this ticket implements):
- A rollout engine that applies suggestion changes using a staged percentage (canary) schedule with configurable ramps (e.g., 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%).
- Canary policy primitives: traffic selection by tenant, route, model version, and synthetic traffic groups; TTL-based promotion criteria; automated rollback triggers tied to metric thresholds.
- Approval workflow: suggestions flagged as "auto-apply eligible" trigger a Console card and an optional Slack review for operators. For changes with higher risk (user-specified thresholds or >X% estimated latency impact), require explicit approve button in Console or an approvals Slack command.
- Monitoring & SLO checks: tie to existing Console dashboards and implement short-window alerts (5m/15m) for latency, 95th and 99th percentiles, error rate increase, and quality regression signals (prompt-set evals).
- Safe-apply orchestration: persist a reversible plan in Optimize history (includes pre-change snapshot, diff of runtime config, and rollout plan) so operators can force-roll back or re-run.
- Audit trail: record who approved or initiated auto-apply, with links to PRs and the pre/post perf snapshots.

Acceptance criteria:
- Rollout engine can run an automated 4-step canary and promote or rollback based on thresholds defined in the canary policy.
- Console UI shows the pending suggestion, rollout progress, metrics for each step, and a single-click rollback.
- Slack/Webhook integration can send the approval card and accept /reject actions, and logs the decision back to the Optimize plan.
- Test harness that simulates 3 workload classes (latency-sensitive, cost-sensitive, mixed) and validates auto-apply will not promote if 95th latency regresses >10% or error rate increases by >0.5pp.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- We will favor routing-based canaries (traffic split) over model-copying for most customers to avoid model duplication costs. For customers who require strict isolation, the policy will allow a model-copy approach as an opt-in which clones the model version in a dedicated pool.
- Rollout window durations are configurable but default to conservative values (30m per step) to allow stable metric observation. Faster rollouts can be configured by SREs for low-risk changes.
- Quality regressions detection leverages existing evals pipelines; however, end-to-end evaluation of generated content in production will be heuristic and may have false positives. We will prioritize high-precision signals for automatic rollback and leave noisy signals for operator review.

Implementation notes:
- New service: optimize-rollout-manager (stateless control plane + persisted RolloutPlan in Optimize datastore).
- Use existing routing layer hooks to implement percentage-based traffic split. Add an API to apply "optimize plan" that accepts rollout steps and threshold rules.
- Metrics: extend Console ingest to attach tags for rollout_id and canary_step so dashboards and alerts can drill down.
- Persist snapshots: store pre-change runtime config (JSON blob) and a checksum for quick integrity checks.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for rollout-state machine (promote, hold, rollback) and policy evaluator.
- Integration test that applies a recommendation to a synthetic tenant and asserts that the 95th latency and error rate metrics are monitored and rollback occurs when thresholds are exceeded.
- Chaos test: during a canary step, introduce artificial GPU contention and ensure rollback triggers.

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood/internal/optimize/auto-apply-rollouts (draft)
- GH PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/421 (rollout manager), https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/994 (UI card)
- Dashboard prototype: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/optimize-rollouts/plan-ENG-5127

Open questions:
1) How do we represent multi-config changes (batching + cache + quantization) in a single atomic plan vs. multiple coordinated plans? Current plan design supports multiple keys but requires a single promotion/rollback path; product may prefer independent release tracks.
2) Approval policy granularity: should approvals be per-tenant, per-project, or global? MVP will be per-tenant with a global admin override.
3) How to estimate downstream cost savings precisely and avoid incentives that promote risky config changes? Need input from finance and product on minimum confidence thresholds.

Next steps:
- Complete rollout-manager prototype and wire basic traffic-split hooks (owner: Miguel).
- Add canary policy schema to Optimize API and update Console card to support approve/reject (owner: Priya + Samir).
- Schedule 2-day testbed run with 3 synthetic tenants (owner: SRE) and iterate on default thresholds.

If you review this ticket, please check the canary policy schema in GH PR 421 and the Console card mock in the Confluence page.
